pages: In the foreground a scrubbed kitchen table in a farm house: an upturned bread bowl over one white sheet of paper blotched with ink. Middle distance, through the open door, Bakki the bay cart horse stands in the yard. Background: a low stone field wall, a hedge, a cart shed. Grey afternoon light lies in one bar across the boards.

Foreground: an old man's hands, knuckles gone stiff and yellow, lying flat on a squared cart shaft. Middle distance, Bakki the bay cart horse of fourteen, one white sock on the near hind, stands at a low stone wall. Background: the cart shed, the meadow, grey drizzle off flat fields.

In a stone byre, Bram, a boy of fifteen with dark hair and a faded red-and-cream striped wool jersey, kneels on the straw with an awl, a trace strap and beeswax. Bakki's head is over the stall door; cows shift in the dark behind, and fading light lies in one strip on the floor.

Bakki's ears turn and his head swings round to the boy in the byre doorway, straw at the corner of his mouth. Bram, fifteen, dark-haired, in the faded red-and-cream striped wool jersey, stands with an awl still raised in one hand and his lips shut. Light comes in low and sideways; the cows are only shapes.

Foreground: a two-wheeled handcart under a wet tarpaulin, clay pots and a tin of lamp oil; the thin man of fifty in a dust-coloured coat sits on its tailboard. Middle distance: Bakki, the bay cart horse with one white sock on the near hind, square at the low stone wall. Bram stands in the lane, hands empty. Flat grey rain.

In the foreground one cracked iron wagon hoop, forty-four inches across, stands against the low stone wall with its broken top soft and leaning, the rain ticking on it. A thin man's hand is on the iron. Bram, fifteen, in the faded red-and-cream striped wool jersey, stands in the wet lane with both arms round it.

The thin man of fifty in the dust-coloured coat holds out a pair of stiff new leather traces. Bakki the bay cart horse waits at the wall. Bram, fifteen, in the faded red-and-cream striped wool jersey, takes them with both hands; a split trace with a green buckle lies on the cart. Cold moonlight on the wet lane.

A boy of thirteen in a brown coat two sizes too big, sleeves turned back, sits on the tailboard of the handcart with a twist of cord looped round the side rail. The thin man's hand is still on the rail above his head. Bakki the bay cart horse stands at the wall; Bram watches from the lane.

The thin man of fifty in the dust-coloured coat has taken his hand off the rail and turned to look at Bakki, the bay cart horse standing square at the low stone wall with one white sock on the near hind. Bram, fifteen, in the faded red-and-cream striped wool jersey, stands in the lane. Flat rain, nothing moved.

Bram, fifteen, in the faded red-and-cream striped wool jersey and a leather apron, sits on a low stone wall under the eaves with his hands hanging between his knees. The cart stands behind him and Bakki is a shape in the dark yard. Sky going grey at the top of the wall; one lit window in the byre.

A grown man's stiff yellow-knuckled hand lies flat on the white sheet of paper on the kitchen table, its face blotched with ink, the bread bowl pushed aside. Bram, fifteen, in the faded red-and-cream striped wool jersey, stands at the table's edge. Through the window: the shed, the low stone wall, frost in the cart ruts. Flat morning light.

Bram, fifteen, in the faded red-and-cream striped wool jersey, comes up the lane toward the handcart, hands open at his sides. The thin man in the dust-coloured coat stands beside the tailboard, and the boy of thirteen in the too-big brown coat sits on the rail. Bakki the bay cart horse holds at the wall. Dusk on wet stone.

In the byre doorway, Bram, fifteen, in the faded red-and-cream striped wool jersey, stands beside his sister Ilma, eleven, in a mustard pinafore over a white shirt with her dark hair plaited. Before them is Bakki's empty stall: swept straw, the halter on its hook, the gate standing open. Low grey morning light through the doorway.

Ilma, eleven, in her mustard pinafore over a white shirt, dark hair plaited, stands at the stall door with one hand on the post, talking to Bram, fifteen, in the faded red-and-cream striped wool jersey. Behind them the empty stall and the open gate. One lantern on the wall; the rest of the byre is dark.

On the kitchen table Bram, fifteen, in the faded red-and-cream striped wool jersey, has opened a brown envelope beside one white sheet blotched with ink; two lines on it are divided by a long ruled rule, and his finger lies along that rule. The bread bowl sits on the shelf. Grey window light, one clear shadow of his hand.

One new iron hoop under the near wheel of a cart down the coast road in April. Eilif walks on the near side with a twist of cord at his wrist; Bram, sixteen, in the red-and-cream striped wool jersey and leather apron, holds the reins. Bakki the bay cart horse walks the far side, the white sock going.

At a stile Bakki the bay cart horse has put his nose over the wall and stands there, one white sock on the near hind showing; Eilif has stopped beside him. Bram, sixteen, in the red-and-cream striped wool jersey and leather apron, sits on the cart with the reins loose on his knees. Thaw light on the hills.

In the foreground a bare larch stake stands by the stone byre door, its groove planed off and its small iron plate nailed back on. Onni, forty, heavy-shouldered, black hair going grey, in a dark blue work coat, drives a nail into the wood with a hammer, his cracked hands steady. Background: black hills. Clear cold light.

Onni, forty, heavy-shouldered, black hair going grey, in a dark blue work coat and wet boots, stands at the edge of a field where a foot of grey ice has sealed the dead barley flat, his scythe on the crust. Middle distance: the low stone byre, a bare larch stake by its door. Background: black hills. Flat white light.

A tall thin figure in a long white coat stands inside the farm gate, hands loose at its sides. Middle distance: Onni, forty, heavy-shouldered, black hair going grey, in a dark blue work coat, beside a barrow of stones on the flagstones. Background: the low stone byre, the bare larch stake, black hills. Low sun and one long cold shadow.

In the middle of a ploughed field, Onni, forty, heavy-shouldered, black hair going grey, in a dark blue work coat, kneels over one grey clay jar the size of a churn, its sailcloth half off, and puts the heel of his hand on the seal. Frost silver at the furrows behind. Flat cold evening light and no shadow. From the window side, the light behind the subject.

Rows of barley six inches high stand in the low field, green-grey like a wet slate roof. Middle distance: Onni, forty, heavy-shouldered, black hair going grey, in a dark blue work coat, stands at the gate talking to a dozen people come off the road. His mattock is stuck in the row behind him. Bright hard frost light.

Long ridges of cut sheaves stand black and glossy on the stubble of the low field. Foreground: the cart stopped at the gate, its shafts down. Middle distance: Onni, forty, heavy-shouldered, black hair going grey, in a dark blue work coat, sits on the cart seat with the reins. Background: the low stone byre, black hills. Low evening sun.

Halla, grey-haired, in a red shawl over a black apron, drives a nail into a bare larch stake with a hammer, her left hand braced flat on the wood. Middle: the stake already black with driven nails in a long line, a small plate nailed at its head. Background: an open byre door and a cold grey day. Seen from a low angle at the level of the stake.

In the darkening yard Halla, grey-haired, in a red shawl over a black apron, counts nails into her palm and then drives the last of them into the larch stake by the stone byre door. A short gap in the line of nails stands open above her hand. The byre window has one lamp in it. Cold blue dusk light.

On a cellar shelf stand rows of preserve jars. At the back, where the shelf goes into the dark, is the grey clay jar the size of a churn. Foreground: Halla, grey-haired, in a red shawl over a black apron, draws a short chalk line on the stone wall beside the shelf. Lamplight from the stair.

Six people walk a wet lane in a north wind, their coats soaked. Middle distance: Halla, grey-haired, in a red shawl over a black apron, keeps to the pace of the slowest, an old man in his shirtsleeves from the low house. Foreground: boots, mud and the frozen edge of a ditch. Background: black hills. Grey light with sleet.

A bare ash tree stands by a boundary stone in the gateway. Halla, grey-haired, in a red shawl over a black apron, stands at the trunk with a sack held against her chest; the grey clay jar is inside it and its shape shows. The lane runs down and up and there is nobody on it. Moonlight and cloud.

At night a white ridge of rime stands along the north side of the ash tree in the gateway. Middle distance: Onni, forty, heavy-shouldered, black hair going grey, in shirtsleeves, stands under it with his arms hanging. In the lit window, a boy of ten in a grey wool sweater presses his face to the glass. Cold blue moonlight.

In the lane Onni, forty, heavy-shouldered, black hair going grey, in a dark blue work coat, lays a stick on the road, a cord beside it and a piece of chalk in his fingers. The fingerpost's shadow lies across the road, and he measures it against the stick's own shadow. Bare hedges, hard frost. Low clear light.

Two oxen stand harnessed outside the low stone byre, a stranger in a brown coat taking the leading ropes. Onni, forty, heavy-shouldered, black hair going grey, in a dark blue work coat, stands at the wall with his hands behind his back. One stall inside the byre is already bare. Overcast flat light, snow at the gate.

In the low field thin pale shoots come up between the furrows and are caught under a fresh sheet of ice. Middle distance: Onni, forty, heavy-shouldered, black hair going grey, in a dark blue work coat, drives the horse over the top field, the drill making straight lines behind him. The low field lies white under snow. Flat winter light.

Onni, forty, heavy-shouldered, black hair going grey, in shirtsleeves, sits on a horse's stall beam in a dark byre with a grey cart horse's head resting against his knee. Middle: a lamp on the wall, a bridle on a nail. Background: dark boards and one doorway of cold light. Seen from just inside the doorway, the doorframe dark at the edge.

One grey clay jar, empty and unstoppered, stands in the middle of a scrubbed kitchen table. Middle distance: snow on the window sill, a cup set down, two chairs either side and both of them empty. Background: a plain wall and a lamp, plain even lamplight. Close on the jar, the room soft behind it. Nobody in the picture.
